reason: A is clearly more crafted: a good serif headline, an illustration, and a tidy button stack with a quiet email link. It ignores dark mode and Dynamic Type, though; its three columns are identical. B adapts properly to dark mode, but its light layout leaves a big empty gap, and at AX-XL it breaks: a clipped 'Continue' overlaps, and the Google/email buttons are pushed off screen.

B looks more art-directed: an illustration, a serif headline and a tight button stack. But it has no dark mode, ignores Dynamic Type, recolors the Apple button off-HIG and uses tiny legal text. A has a real dark mode with an inverted Apple button and does scale with text size. Its AX-XL layout breaks, though: a clipped 'Continue' and buttons pushed offscreen. It also mixes rectangle and pill button shapes and leaves a large dead gap.

A is the richer, better-art-directed page (inline size grid, swatches, brand content), but it ignores dark mode and Dynamic Type: its dark and AX-XL screenshots match light mode. B uses a native nav bar with glass buttons and list rows, and has a real dark mode with an inverted CTA. B's text scales at AX-XL, though the rating gets clipped under the CTA.

B is richer: visible size grid, swatches, size guide, a brand voice. But it ignores dark mode and Dynamic Type entirely. Its dark and AX-XL columns look the same as light, its text is tiny, and it has a ghost 'TR' watermark and a hand-rolled header. A is restrained and native, with a real dark mode, and it scales text, though the rating line clips at AX-XL.

B ignores dark mode and Dynamic Type: its dark and AX-XL screens look the same as light. Its custom tab bar overlaps content, with 'Recent activity' showing below it and clipped budget amounts. Its card-heavy layout uses 'US$' throughout. A is restrained, with a single dominant figure, and it adapts to dark mode and AX-XL, though the AX-XL budget/spent stack is oddly indented.

A has no dark mode and ignores Dynamic Type: all three columns look identical. Its custom tab bar overlaps and clips the budget amounts, and 'Recent activity' renders under the bar. It mixes US$ and $ formats. B adapts to dark mode and scales at AX-XL with one restrained accent and realistic content. Its stat block indents oddly at AX-XL.

B has a more distinctive brand and richer content, but its dark-mode and AX-XL shots look the same as light mode: no dark theme and no Dynamic Type. Its custom floating tab bar overlaps the list. A is plain but native. Its dark mode uses proper surface steps and its text scales at AX-XL, although the filter chips get cut off there.

A looks more branded: a serif title, a green balance card and cents set smaller than dollars. But its dark mode is identical to light, its text does not scale at AX-XL, its captions are tiny and low-contrast, and list rows show through under the floating tab bar. B is more native. Its dark mode has surface steps, and at AX-XL its rows reflow, with only the filter chips running off the edge.

B ignores dark mode: it stays the same cream screen. It also ignores Dynamic Type, since at AX-XL only the logo icon grows. B's tilted cards, sparkles and clipped quote text add decoration that doesn't earn its place. A has a real dark palette, text that scales at AX-XL (the card scrolls under the CTA), and a restrained headline-first layout. Its weak spot is a large empty gap above the CTA.

A ignores dark mode entirely (stays cream) and doesn't scale at AX-XL; tilted overlapping cards clip the quote text and the decorative stars add noise, though its serif headline is lovely. B adapts properly to dark mode, scales its type (the card clips under a pinned CTA, so presumably it scrolls), stays restrained and has specific, domain-true sample content.

A has the more crafted look (serif, illustration, tinted selected card), but its dark and AX-XL columns are identical to light: no dark mode and no Dynamic Type. It also has no close or restore control, and the legal line is clipped. B adapts to dark mode, scales text with a pinned CTA, and has native close, restore and terms controls.

B has a stronger brand feel (serif headline, illustration), but it ignores dark mode and Dynamic Type: the dark and AX-XL screens are pixel-identical to light. It also has no close or Restore button, and its legal text is tiny and clipped. A is plain but native: it has close and Restore, a pinned CTA, a working dark mode, real AX-XL scaling and clear terms.

A has more character: serif title and a strong Plus hero card. But it ignores Dynamic Type entirely (the AX-XL view is unchanged), and in dark mode the Explore Plus label is unreadable on its light pill. B is restrained, native inset-grouped iOS and scales properly at AX-XL. Its weak spots are a flat hierarchy and an odd footer caption.

A is a restrained, native inset-grouped list that scales at AX-XL (a few awkward wraps, and a footer crowds the next header). B ignores Dynamic Type entirely. Its dark mode has illegible 'Explore Plus' text and pure-black cards on a green background. It also leans on decoration: eyebrow caps, serif, promo card. Its 2-3 tracked-caps captions are tiny.

B's dark-mode and AX-XL screenshots look the same as its light-mode one. It ignores dark appearance and Dynamic Type, and its 8–9pt eyebrow labels and captions have low contrast. A has a restrained single-accent hierarchy, a native large title and segmented control, and a properly adjusted dark mode. Its text scales at AX-XL, though the chart axis labels get oversized. B's stat cards are bordering on card soup.

A looks polished in light mode: a strong hero card, lime accent and good data. But its dark and AX-XL renders are identical to light, so it ignores dark mode and Dynamic Type entirely. It also has an icon-heavy tile row and a custom header, and its 2024 dates are stale. B uses a native large title and segmented control, a disciplined orange accent and proper dark surfaces, and its text scales at AX-XL.
